title: Tauri Architecture & IPC
objectives: Trace one command round-trip end to end
Explain why events are optional here
body:
# Tauri Architecture & IPC

## Two worlds, one window

```text
┌ WebView (Vue) ────────┐        ┌ Rust core ─────────┐
│ UI · stores · ipc.ts  │ ⇄ IPC ⇄ │ commands → services │
└───────────────────────┘        │ → SQLite/exec       │
                                 └─────────────────────┘
```

The webview renders; the Rust process owns everything privileged: filesystem,
SQLite, child processes. The boundary is a typed command surface.

## Anatomy of one call

```ts
// frontend
const result = await invoke<RunResult>('run_rust_code', { code })
//            ↓ serialized as JSON over IPC bridge
```rust
#[tauri::command]
async fn run_rust_code(code: String) -> Result<RunResult, AppError> { … }
```

Arg names convert camelCase↔snake_case automatically; return values serialize
via serde. Errors cross as structured objects when `AppError: Serialize`.
This app's `src/services/ipc.ts` + `src-tauri/src/commands/*` are the living
reference.

## Events vs request/response

Events (`emit`/`listen`) suit push updates (progress ticks). This app chooses
pure request/response: every interaction is an awaited call — simpler to test,
no hidden ordering. Choose events only when true push semantics exist.

## Where state lives Rust-side

`app.manage(AppState)` registers types retrievable via `State<T>` parameters.
One DB connection behind a mutex; execution registry for cancellation — see
`src-tauri/src/state.rs`.
